pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
> 📐 **Strand 3 — Geometry And Measurement**
Shape, space, measurement, position and movement — the mathematics of the world around us.

> 🎯 **Content standard** (B9.3.1)
- B9.3.1.1 — Apply the properties of angles at a point, angles on a straight line, vertically opposite angles, and corresponding and alternate angles to solve problems.

> 🎯 **In this chapter you will learn to:**
- name polygons and derive the formula (n − 2) × 180° for the sum of their interior angles
- calculate missing interior and exterior angles of polygons
- recognise similar and congruent triangles and state the conditions for congruence
- use similarity and congruence to find unknown sides and angles

pages.title: Angle sums of polygons
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Derive the formula for calculating the sum of angles in any polygon and use it to calculate the values of missing angles in polygons.
Curriculum indicator B9.3.1.1.1
| **Number of sides** | **3** | **4** | **5** | **6** | **7** | **8** | **9** | **10** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Name | triangle | quadrilateral | pentagon | hexagon | heptagon | octagon | nonagon | decagon |
> 🔑 **Key idea: Interior angle sum** — From one vertex of an n-sided polygon, diagonals divide it into **(n − 2)** triangles. So the **sum of the interior angles = (n − 2) × 180°**. For a **regular** polygon each interior angle = [[(n − 2) × 180°/n]] and each exterior angle = [[360°/n]].
[[fig:m9-f14|Figure 8.1: Dividing polygons into triangles from one vertex]]
## ✏️ Example 8.1
Use the formula to find x in each polygon.
[[fig:m9-f15]]
Figure 8.2: Find x
**Solution**
a) Triangle: (3 − 2) × 180° = 180°. x + 2x + 60° = 180° ⟹ 3x = 120° ⟹ **x = 40°**
b) Quadrilateral: (4 − 2) × 180° = 360°. 110° + 75° + x + (x + 25°) = 360° ⟹ 2x = 150° ⟹ **x = 75°**
c) Pentagon: 540°. 120° + 95° + 2x + 3x + 100° = 540° ⟹ 5x = 225° ⟹ **x = 45°** (angles 120°, 95°, 90°, 135°, 100°)
## ✏️ Example 8.2
A hexagon has angles x, x + 10°, x + 20°, x + 30°, x + 40° and x + 50°. Find x and the angles.
**Solution**
Sum = (6 − 2) × 180° = 720°. 6x + 150° = 720° ⟹ **x = 95°**. The angles are 95°, 105°, 115°, 125°, 135° and 145°.

pages.title: Similar and congruent triangles
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Identify similar and congruent triangles and use the knowledge to solve related problems.
Curriculum indicator B9.3.1.1.2
> 🔑 **Key idea: Similar triangles** — Triangles are **similar** if their corresponding **angles are equal**; then their corresponding **sides are in the same ratio** (the scale factor). If △ABC ~ △PQR, then [[PQ/AB]] = [[QR/BC]] = [[PR/AC]].
> 🔑 **Key idea: Congruent triangles** — Triangles are **congruent** (≡) if they are exactly the same shape and size. Two triangles are congruent if any one of these holds: **SSS** (three sides equal); **SAS** (two sides and the included angle equal); **ASA** (two angles and a corresponding side equal); **RHS** (right angle, hypotenuse and one other side equal).
[[fig:m9-f16|Figure 8.3: Conditions for congruence]]
## ✏️ Example 8.3
Triangles ABC and ADE are similar (DE ∥ BC). AD = 4 cm, AB = 10 cm, DE = 6 cm and ∠ADE = 65°. Find BC and ∠ABC.
[[fig:m9-f17]]
Figure 8.4: DE is parallel to BC
**Solution**
Because DE ∥ BC, ∠ADE = ∠ABC (corresponding angles) and ∠A is common, so △ADE ~ △ABC.
∠ABC = ∠ADE = **65°**
Scale factor = [[AB/AD]] = [[10/4]] = 2.5, so BC = 2.5 × DE = 2.5 × 6 = **15 cm**
## ✏️ Example 8.4
In the diagram, AB = AD and ∠BAC = ∠DAC. Show that △ABC ≡ △ADC and find x and y.
[[fig:m9-f18]]
Figure 8.5: Is △ABC congruent to △ADC?
**Solution**
AB = AD (given), ∠BAC = ∠DAC (given) and AC is common. So △ABC ≡ △ADC (**SAS**).
Corresponding parts are equal: BC = DC ⟹ **x = 7 cm**, and ∠ACB = ∠ACD ⟹ **y = 38°**.

pages.title: Example 8.5
pages.body:
## ✏️ Example 8.5
Find x using similar triangles: a vertical pole 2 m high casts a shadow 3 m long. At the same time a tree casts a shadow 18 m long. How tall is the tree?
**Solution**
[[fig:m9-f19]]
Figure 8.6: The pole and the tree form similar triangles
The sun's rays make equal angles with the ground, so the triangles are similar.
[[x/2]] = [[18/3]] ⟹ x = 2 × 6 = **12 m**

pages.title: Exercise 8.2
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Exercise 8.2** — try these on paper or in your head, then tap **Quick check** to see the answers.
1. Two triangles have angles 40°, 60°, 80° and 80°, 40°, 60°. Are they similar? Must they be congruent?
2. △PQR ~ △XYZ with PQ = 6 cm, QR = 8 cm, PR = 9 cm and XY = 9 cm. Find YZ and XZ.
3. State the condition (SSS, SAS, ASA or RHS) that proves each pair congruent: a) sides 5, 7, 9 and 9, 5, 7 b) right-angled, hypotenuse 13, one side 5 in both c) sides 6 and 8 with included angle 50° in both.
4. A ladder 5 m long reaches 4 m up a wall. A similar ladder reaches 6 m up the wall at the same angle. How long is it?
5. A man 1.8 m tall stands 12 m from a lamp post and casts a shadow 4 m long. How high is the lamp?

questions.q: Two triangles have angles 40°, 60°, 80° and 80°, 40°, 60°. Are they similar? Must they be congruent?

parts.a: Yes, similar (equal angles). Not necessarily congruent — the sizes may differ.

pages.title: Chapter 8 summary
pages.body:
- Sum of interior angles = (n − 2) × 180°; exterior angles sum to 360°.
- Similar: equal angles, proportional sides. Congruent: same shape and size (SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS).
